hints: `map` doubles the value inside a `Some`; `filter` turns `Some` into `None` if the test fails.
exercises.solution: a: `Some(4)` becomes `Some(8)`, which passes the filter (8 > 5), so `a` is 8. b: `Some(2)` becomes `Some(4)`, which fails the filter and becomes `None`, so `b` is the default 0. c: `map` does nothing to `None`, so `c` is −1. Output: `8 0 -1`.

exercises.prompt: A `Playlist` struct needs a method `shuffle` that reorders its songs in place. Which first parameter should it take?

options.label: `&self`
options.feedback: Not yet. A shared borrow cannot change the playlist's fields.

options.label: `&mut self`
options.feedback: Yes. Shuffling changes the playlist but the caller keeps it afterwards, so a mutable borrow is exactly right.

options.label: `self`
options.feedback: Not yet. Taking ownership would consume the playlist; the caller would need it returned to keep using it.

options.label: No `self` at all: make it an associated function.
options.feedback: Not yet. Associated functions such as `new` don't operate on an existing value; `shuffle` does.

hints: Does the method change the value? Does the caller still have it afterwards?
exercises.solution: `shuffle` modifies the playlist and the caller keeps using it, so it takes `&mut self`. `&self` is for methods that only read, and `self` for methods that consume or transform the value into something else.

hints: What range of values does a `u8` hold?
exercises.solution: "42" parses into a `u8`, so the first result is `Ok(42)` and `is_ok()` is `true`. 300 is larger than 255, the largest `u8`, so parsing fails with an error and `is_err()` is also `true`. Output: `true true`.

exercises.prompt: A traffic light controller stores `struct Light { red: bool, amber: bool, green: bool }`. Which redesign best makes illegal states unrepresentable?

options.label: `enum Light { Red, RedAmber, Green, Amber }`
options.feedback: Yes. Exactly the four real phases exist, and nothing like "red and green at once" can be built.

options.label: Keep the struct and add a method `is_valid(&self) -> bool`.
options.feedback: Not yet. The invalid states still exist; every user must remember to call the check.

options.label: `struct Light { phase: u8 }` with a comment explaining 0 to 3.
options.feedback: Not yet. 252 of the 256 possible values are meaningless, and the compiler can't help with any of them.

options.label: `struct Light { colours: Vec<String> }`
options.feedback: Not yet. This allows even more nonsense, such as "purple" or no colours at all.

hints: Three booleans allow 8 combinations. How many of them are real phases of a traffic light?
exercises.solution: Three booleans can represent 8 states, of which only a few are real phases. An enum with one variant per real phase makes the others impossible to construct, and every `match` on it is checked for exhaustiveness. Validation methods and integers leave the bad states representable.

exercises.prompt: Why does `#[derive(Clone, Copy)]` work on `struct Celsius(f64);` but fail on `struct Book { title: String, year: u16 }`?

options.label: A type can be `Copy` only if all its fields are `Copy`, and `String` is not, because it owns heap memory.
options.feedback: Yes. Copying a String's three words would create two owners of one heap block, so String implements only `Clone`.

options.label: Tuple structs can be `Copy`; structs with named fields cannot.
options.feedback: Not yet. Named-field structs can be `Copy` too, as long as every field is.

options.label: `u16` is not `Copy`.
options.feedback: Not yet. All the primitive integer types are `Copy`.

options.label: Structs with more than one field are too big to copy.
options.feedback: Not yet. Size has nothing to do with it; a `[u8; 1000]` array is `Copy`.

hints: What would it mean to copy a String bit for bit?
exercises.solution: `Copy` means "duplicating the bits is a complete, safe copy". That holds for `f64` but not for `String`, whose bits include a pointer to a heap block it owns: two bitwise copies would both try to free it. So `String` is `Clone` (an explicit deep copy) but not `Copy`, and any struct containing one cannot derive `Copy`. `Book` can still derive `Clone`.
